title: Mantle - embeddings & rerank discovery
next_steps: Send Hosted vs Dedicated pricing sheet
Schedule dedicated capacity demo with benchmarks (week of Mar 9)
Run small 10k-vector benchmark with Mantle dataset
action_items: Lena Park: send pricing + security pack (due: 2026-03-06)
Marcus Reed: propose benchmark config + scripts (due: 2026-03-09)
Diego Martinez: share sample data subset and current embedding pipeline (due: 2026-03-05)
summary: Discovery to understand Mantle's reranking workflow: embedding dimensionality, vector DB choice, throughput targets, and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment fits their security and latency needs. Agreed to run a small benchmark and follow up with pricing and security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm lena from Redwood. quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya Shah: Priya here, Head of Search at Mantle.
[00:08] Diego Martinez: Diego, ML eng on the search team.
[00:10] Aaron Cole: Aaron, CTO.
[00:12] Marcus Reed: Marcus, i'm the solutions engineer at Redwood.
[00:18] Lena Park: Awesome. Goal for today is to understand your current rerank stack, constraints, and timeline. we'll cover hosted vs dedicated vs private as it relates to embeddings and rerank.
[00:30] Priya Shah: sweet. quick background: we run a hybrid search — elastic for inverted index + vector for semantic layer. we currently generate 1536-d embeddings using an in-house model, store in Pinecone, and then run an ANN rerank.
[00:46] Diego Martinez: yes, end-to-end latency target is sub 150ms P95 for our product search rerank. throughput during black friday-ish peaks is ~1200 qps sustained for 10-15 minutes, baseline typical 200-300 qps.
[01:05] Marcus Reed: okay that helps — when you say 1536 dims, what batch sizes do you do for embedding generation and inference?
[01:12] Diego Martinez: generation is batched offline; online we embed single queries. for rerank we score top-200 candidates with a cross-encoder on GPU right now, but that's getting expensive. looking at two-stage: dense retrieval via vector DB then light rerank model.
[01:30] Priya Shah: cost is big driver — cloud bills spiking. also want tighter SLOs. curious about Redwood's Hosted and Dedicated options and whether you support on-prem or VPC for customer data.
[01:44] Lena Park: yep. short answer: Hosted is fastest to get started — managed, per-token/per-embedding pricing. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and autoscaling, good for your peak qps; Private (VPC/on-prem) supports stricter compliance and data isolation.
[02:02] Marcus Reed: technical note: our runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache management to lower per-token time and cost. for embeddings, we support returning raw vectors (various dims) and can integrate with existing vector DBs via connector or you can host vectors in Redwood's store for lower round-trip.
[02:22] Aaron Cole: can you integrate with Pinecone? we've already invested there, switching is non-trivial.
[02:26] Marcus Reed: absolutely — we have connectors for Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, and S3-backed vector stores. we can either push vectors from your pipeline into whatever DB, or host vectors in Redwood and use a hybrid routing approach.
[02:40] Priya Shah: hybrid routing? clarify.
[02:42] Lena Park: by hybrid search we mean combining lexical scoring and vector similarity — typical approach is first-pass keyword filter (elastic) then vector nearest-neighbors then rerank. Redwood can orchestrate the flow and do prefix caching to speed up hot queries. also we support mixing signal types in rerank stage.
[02:58] Diego Martinez: what's the dimensionality tradeoff? we get better quality with 1536 but that's heavier for ANN and storage. any recommendations?
[03:06] Marcus Reed: common guidance: 768 or 1024 hits good balance if model quality acceptable — but depends on your model. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and dimensionality profiles based on a sample workload; we can run a small eval comparing 768/1024/1536 for recall and downstream rerank delta.
[03:25] Priya Shah: sweet. throughput — you mentioned dedicated pools, can you give ballpark throughput for top-K retrieval + light rerank? we need to model cost for 1200 qps peaks.
[03:36] Marcus Reed: rough numbers: if you keep ANN in a separate vector DB (Pinecone/Milvus), retrieval latency is dominated by DB and network; with Dedicated, we can guarantee X qps for embedding/rerank paths by reserving GPUs. a light rerank model (smaller transformer) can do ~200-400 qps per GPU depending on batch and sequence length; with batching and continuous KV caching you can raise effective throughput. exact numbers depend on rerank model size, sequence length, and batchability.
[04:05] Aaron Cole: so we'd likely keep Pinecone for retrieval and use Redwood for hosting rerank model? or host both? pros/cons?
[04:12] Lena Park: both are options. keep Pinecone for retrieval to avoid migration cost; Redwood can call Pinecone for k-NN then run the reranker on Dedicated. If you want single-provider latency optimization we can host vectors here (reducing cross-network), but that increases storage on our side — usually recommended when latency is critical and you want more control.
[04:33] Priya Shah: security: we need SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs, and option for VPC peering. do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:41] Marcus Reed: yes: SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC-only control planes. we'll share the security pack after this call.
[04:55] Diego Martinez: can we run a benchmark with our sample dataset? we'd like to see P95 latency for retrieval+rerank for 200/400/1200 qps.
[05:03] Marcus Reed: that works — smallest benchmark we recommend 10k vectors and 1k queries to get meaningful numbers. we'll run variants: vectors in Pinecone + Redwood rerank, vectors in Redwood + Redwood rerank, and varied dims 768/1024/1536.
[05:21] Priya Shah: cost modeling — curious about Dedicated commit sizes and burst capacity. we don't want to overcommit but also need predictable performance.
[05:29] Lena Park: Dedicated has monthly commitments with autoscale and burst options. we can propose a standing pool sized for your base and configure burst to handle short peaks. pricing sheet i'll send outlines typical commit tiers and cost/per-qps modeling.
[05:43] Aaron Cole: timeline: we're evaluating partners now, want a pilot by end of Q2. data residency might be required for EU customers — can Redwood meet that?
[05:53] Marcus Reed: yes, we have regional deployments and Private options for EU residency. for Hosted we also have EU regions. we'll capture your residency constraints in the follow up.
[06:03] Diego Martinez: any gotchas with dimensionality and ANN index params? e.g., recall drop when reducing dims and needing to increase ef/search params which raises latency.
[06:12] Marcus Reed: that's accurate. reducing dims reduces index size and speeds distance calc but can lower recall; you may need to adjust ef/ef_search or nprobes, which increases CPU/latency. our Optimize tool will benchmark and recommend a sweet spot. also quantization (int8/4-bit) can reduce memory with modest quality loss — again, workload dependent.
[06:34] Priya Shah: integration work — how intrusive is it to hook into our current pipeline (elastic + Pinecone + internal rerank)?
[06:42] Lena Park: usually low: we integrate via API calls. options: 1) Redwood orchestrates post-retrieval rerank — you keep current retrieval from elastic/pinecone and send top-K to Redwood; 2) Redwood replaces rerank and optionally hosts vectors; 3) full migration to Redwood vector store. first two options are quick and low risk.
[06:58] Diego Martinez: ok good. can you send example configs for connectors and sample benchmark repo?
[07:02] Marcus Reed: yes — action item for me. we'll share a benchmark repo with manifest and scripts.
[07:08] Aaron Cole: nothing else from me, looking forward to the security pack and pricing.
[07:12] Priya Shah: one more Q — do you have guidance on embedding refresh cadence for e-commerce product catalog that changes daily?
[07:18] Marcus Reed: incremental updates are typical. use cold + hot layers: full reindex daily, incremental upserts throughout day. Redwood supports partial upserts and prefix caching so hot items get fast lookup.
[07:30] Lena Park: great. recap of next steps: lena send pricing + security docs; marcus share benchmark config + run sample; diego share sample dataset; schedule demo for dedicated capacity. any questions?
[07:43] Priya Shah: nope, thanks.
[07:45] Diego Martinez: thanks everyone.
[07:47] Aaron Cole: thanks.
[07:48] Lena Park: thanks all, we'll follow up shortly.
